cand.title: 2027 OBIO Investment Summit
cand.ledgerVenue: Arcadian Court & Loft, 401 Bay Street, Toronto

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Best named routing contacts: Christina Yeh, Vice President, Programs & Strategic Partnerships (role verified September 2026; named travel-discount contact on the 2023 Summit planning page), and Parnian Tajbakhsh, Senior Manager, Capital Access (official CAAP contact; programme feeds companies into the Summit). Doriane Rey, Senior Manager, Marketing & Communications, is an additional communications referral; Dr. Maura Campbell, President & CEO, is executive sponsorship/escalation. None is verified as the 2027 hotel contract signatory. Start via summit@obio.ca and request the accommodation decision-maker.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced activity dates: February 2–4, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada; within the requested horizon. The dedicated 2027 planning page and OBIO event calendar agree. The calendar URL contains 2026, but its event content explicitly specifies 2027; these are activity dates, not article dates. No 2028 edition announcement was located.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: a city-business lodging opportunity, not a resort buyout. A 157-room Harbourfront hotel could plausibly serve a modest investor, speaker, company-team or VIP allocation while delegates attend Arcadian downtown. This event is not at MTCC or Exhibition Place, so those proximity claims do not establish fit. No published demand supports a specific allocation or the illustrative 15–109 peak-room range. Do not propose exclusive housing or a whole-Summit move: the 2027 venue is already announced and the hotel’s approximately 240-theatre ballroom does not establish adequate Summit-wide capacity. Side meetings are conditional opportunities; catering/receptions require restaurant, staffing and catering verification first.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: Arcadian Court & Loft, 401 Bay Street, Simpson Tower, 8th Floor, Toronto, Ontario M5H 2Y4. This is downtown Toronto proper at Bay/Queen, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. It is an event complex, not a competing hotel. Organizer publication establishes the announced venue, not access to the underlying signed contract.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified history shows destination and format changes, not a fixed city rotation: Niagara-on-the-Lake in 2019–2020; virtual in 2021–2022; Toronto at Lennox Hall in 2023, Schwartz Reisman Innovation Centre in 2024, and Arcadian Court & Loft in 2025–2026, retained for 2027. OBIO calls the Summit annual and documents activity since 2018. Exact 2018 dates and venue remain unverified.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027 lodging pathway is unknown: the dedicated planning page publishes venue and transportation information but no hotel, room block, housing bureau, booking commitment or open hotel RFP. Quote: “The 2027 OBIO® Investment Summit will take place on February 2-4.” Historical 2026 accommodation evidence names ONE hotel: “Hilton Toronto is offering those attending the OBIO® Investment Summit a 10% discount on their Best Available Rate at the time of booking.” This is an edition-specific discount, not a published contracted room block, exclusivity agreement or 2027 commitment. Historical 2019 accommodation was at Pillar and Post Inn & Spa; 2020 company registration included two nights’ accommodation, with hotel name unverified. No current peak-room or room-night figure was found.
findings.organizationStructure: OBIO describes itself as a not-for-profit, membership-based organization founded in 2009. The Summit is an OBIO-owned/organized health-science capital-access and partnering programme, rather than evidence of a corporate incentive trip. Arcadian is the event venue; no external PCO, DMC or housing bureau was identified in the reviewed edition sources. Do not equate the venue operator or investor-programme contacts with the lodging buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Hilton Toronto has a documented 2026 attendee discount relationship; 2027 continuation, exclusivity and allocation are unknown. Arcadian already holds the announced 2027 meeting location. No sourced evidence establishes hotel sell-outs, unmet lodging demand, overflow allocations or displaced delegates. Investor/company counts and partnering-meeting counts are not room demand and must not be added together as attendance.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact summit@obio.ca now, requesting Christina Yeh or the 2027 accommodation lead; use Parnian Tajbakhsh as a programme-side referral. Ask whether 2027 has a contracted hotel/bureau or merely a discount code, whether Hilton continues, whether supplemental hotels may participate, and for non-local delegate/speaker counts, arrival/departure pattern, peak rooms, room nights and decision deadline. If permitted, offer a modest, non-exclusive Radisson accommodation proposal subject to availability; obtain the actual room pattern before quoting a block. Separately request the next-cycle hotel review calendar. Do not pitch replacement of Arcadian for 2027 or promise catering before operational verification.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is a confirmed upcoming edition with its meeting venue announced. Lodging accessibility remains unconfirmed, not closed and not open by default. Approach OBIO for permission to discuss a supplementary accommodation option; do not market Radisson as an official hotel or claim approved inventory. No published evidence shows 2027 lodging committed to Hilton or a bureau.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: annual recurrence and prior hotel-supported destination editions justify relationship development for later Toronto accommodation cycles. Toronto hosting is verified for 2023–2027, but neither a Toronto 2028 edition nor its dates/venue is announced in reviewed sources. Future capture should focus on a modest accommodation allocation and, only if invited, side meetings; historical resort use does not prove a current resort requirement or an open future venue tender.
